distractors.reason: 'Hardly' means almost not or barely. 'I work hardly' means I almost do not work.
'Badly' means poorly or in a bad way. We do not use 'work badly' to describe working with effort.
'Strongly' is not used with 'work' in this sense. The natural partner for effort is 'hard'.

example_sentence: I always work ___ on my project.
l1_interference: Los hispanohablantes a veces traducen 'trabajar fuerte' como 'work strong'. En inglés se dice 'work hard', porque el adverbio 'hard' indica esfuerzo.
explanation: 'Hard' is the adverb that goes with 'work' to show a lot of effort. 'Hard' and 'hardly' look similar but have very different meanings.

related_collocations.example: I study hard before every exam.
Please speak clearly so the examiner can understand you.
Listen carefully to the question before you answer.

memory_tip: WORK HARD = put in a lot of effort | HARDLY = almost not at all
